pairs.difference: B: the gold-foil satellite body sits on a solid orange ring field, and the whole card is one warm family (warm_share 0.95, 1.31 hue families). In the lens the satellite dissolves into the orange, and its blue panels turn brown-orange. A: a yellow player and grey-white earbuds on violet, a clear yellow-against-violet split. It also has few hue families, but hero and ground stay apart.
pairs.fix: Keep the satellite's solar panels a deep cool blue and its body a cool grey-silver. Make the background a softer, less saturated orange so it doesn't flood the object. Add one small cool accent.

pairs.difference: A: the helmet shell is a pinkish cream white with a gold visor on a loud cyan burst. The lens shows the white shell picking up mint from the background. This matches the lessons, where generated cards warm the whites to cream. B: a tan jacket with an orange collar and a dark green sash on green, with believable local colors and green-related shadows. The evidence is weak either way.
pairs.fix: Paint the helmet shell a clean neutral light grey white, not cream or pink. Keep the visor a deeper, less glowing amber.

pairs.difference: A: a grey vault door on a cyan wall and floor. Almost the whole card is one cool blue-grey family, and the only accent is the orange wheel. Subject chroma (0.044) and warm share (0.03) are both below the real-card range. B: a blue door, orange frame, green ivy and a pink, yellow and white wreath, with several local colors balanced against each other the way the real cards do it.
pairs.fix: Give the vault door a warmer gunmetal with some brass on the hinges and bolts. Make the wall a less saturated teal, and add a second warm material, such as a wooden floor or a yellow hazard stripe, so the card isn't all blue-grey.

pairs.difference: B: one large mass of saturated navy on orange wood, with only gold stars. That's a two-family blue-versus-orange card. A: a cream paper map with light blue sea, tan land, small green islands and a grey and black magnifier on wood, a varied, believable palette like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Make the star chart a softer midnight blue with faded paper edges and some muted teal or violet nebula tints. Make the compass a duller brass.

pairs.difference: B: every fruit is at full chroma: red melon, orange slices, lime grapes, red berries. They sit on a warm orange-tan plank floor, so the whole card is warm (0.85) and has no rest area. A: a hot pink flamingo against blue water and a peach tile deck, a clear hero-against-ground hue split.
pairs.fix: Make the wooden table a cooler, greyer wood or put the plate on a light blue cloth. Soften the grapes and oranges a little so one fruit, the watermelon, carries the strongest color.

pairs.difference: B: a grey-white spaceship on a flat lime-green gradient. The subject is almost colorless (chroma 0.028, below the real-card range), and in the lens the hull, shadow and ground all go green, leaving about one hue family (1.15). A: a saturated blue machine on magenta, with red, yellow, green and blue cans inside, so it has local-color variety.
pairs.fix: Paint the spaceship with real local colors: a white hull with red or orange stripes and a blue cockpit glass. Put it on a backdrop of a different hue that's less saturated than lime, with darker, cooler shadows under the ship.

pairs.difference: A: a dark green lamp on a turquoise burst. This is a known real card from the anchor sheet, even though it's nearly monochrome. B: a red cooler with yellow, green and purple cans on yellow sand under a blue sky, with plausible local colors and purple-red shadow. Nothing on this vector marks B as generated.

B: a grey control panel on a saturated yellow-gold wall. The subject has almost no color (0.031), and the card is almost all warm (0.95). In the lens the red buttons and green screen merge into the grey and yellow. A: a light blue fan in front of a green curtain and an orange wall, with a light blue sky through the window. Several hue families, each with a role.
pairs.fix: Make the wall a cooler, less saturated steel blue or teal. Keep the screen a vivid green and the buttons a clear red so the panel has its own color accents.

pairs.difference: B: a silver pouch on a purple striped wall. The foil takes strong purple and orange from its surroundings, its shadows are more saturated than its lit faces (shadow chroma 1.61, above range), and the shadow on the table goes violet. A: red gloves with deep red-maroon shadows on a blue wall and wooden table. The shadows stay in the same hue family and are believable.
pairs.fix: Shade the foil pouch with neutral grey shadows that carry only a slight purple tint. Make the purple wall a deeper, more muted color.

pairs.difference: A: a white rover with black wheels on pale sand under a blue sky. Its subject chroma (0.028) and shadow chroma (0.39) are both below the real-card range. The only color mass is the yellow dish, and the body is an empty neutral. B: the beige computer on an orange wall and wooden desk is a known real card from the lessons.
pairs.fix: Give the rover body a clear local color, such as orange or teal panels with a white trim. Shade the wheels dark blue-grey. Make the sand a warmer ochre and the sky a deeper blue so the hero has its own hue.

pairs.difference: B: white mitts on a violet gradient. The whites, shadows and floor all go purple in the lens, giving 1.36 hue families, a warm share of 0.05 and shadow chroma of 1.74, above range. The small orange bands are the only break. A: blue shoes with green and teal laces on orange and cream, with several local colors that each hold their place.
pairs.fix: Paint the gloves a neutral light grey white with cool grey shadows, not purple ones. Make the orange cuffs larger, and use a softer, less saturated lavender or another hue for the backdrop.

pairs.difference: A: a white and blue plane in a blue sky with blue-white clouds. The card has no warm color at all (warm share 0.0), and the shadows on the white fuselage go to strong saturated blue (2.24, far above range). B: a white rocket in the same sky, broken by one red accent on the nose and fins and a yellow-orange flame. This is the real cards' habit of one warm accent on a cool card.
pairs.fix: Shade the white fuselage with soft grey-blue, not strong blue. Add one warm accent, such as an orange or red tail stripe or a yellow window band.

pattern: Generated cards tend to turn into one-hue cards. A low-chroma grey or white hero is soaked by a single saturated backdrop, so the hero's shadows, the floor and even its whites take on the background color (green ship, purple mitts, yellow panel, orange satellite). That leaves too few hue families, warm share close to 0 or 1, and shadow chroma higher than on lit faces. The real cards give the hero its own local colors that differ from the background, add one small accent of a different hue, and keep whites neutral.
